newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Chiwan Wharf signs Shenzhen warehouse JV.
newsitem.headline: Chiwan Wharf signs Shenzhen warehouse JV.

text.p: China's Chiwan Wharf Holdings Co Ltd has signed a deal with a Hong Kong firm to form a joint venture to build a cargo warehouse in Shenzhen, a Chiwan official said on Wednesday.

The $27 million Shenzhen Longhua Warehouse Co Ltd joint venture will complete the 150,000 square metre complex by mid 1998, the official told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin. The project carries a 14 percent annual rate of return, he said.
Longhua has a registered capital of $18 million.
Chiwan, which has foreign currency B shares listed in Shenzhen, and Hong Kong-based American Consolidation Services Ltd will each take a 33.3 percent stake in the warehouse, the official said.
Shenzhen Sungang Warehouse Holdings Co Ltd will hold the remaining stake, he said.
American Services is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Hong Kong sports bag maker Pam & Frank International Holdings Ltd.
Chiwan on Monday said its shareholders had approved a plan to make a two-for-10 rights issue tentatively priced at between 4.5 and 6.0 yuan per share.
